directive.quote: An engine fix must reach accounts without any Mac app install.

job: Publish a signed engine release on every push to the branch, so every computer adopts it from a release feed
preserve: The signature domain and the signed release fields retain their exact byte order and separators.
Repository and signing credentials retain their existing descriptor and service-credential boundaries.
First-parent source checks, release antirollback, per-target admission, and the feed's atomic update remain intact.
allowed_deltas: Check the supplied SDK's architecture stubs before replacing the builder's prior SDK.
banned_substitutions: Renaming an existing consumer's public signature domain or build metadata variables to make source generic.

distinct_from.why: This tool itself: its README, rows, settings and tests name the signing domain, the release values and the push signature header it uses.
This tool's own capability row, whose owner names this folder: the registry entry for this tool, not another owner of the job.
The generated tool catalog (publish-tool-catalog.mjs): it carries this tool's own rows. A generated listing of this tool, not another owner of the job.
start-a-computer writes the release_feed a computer reads this tool's feed with, and its README names this folder as the feed's publisher; it starts places and publishes nothing.

The older product's Workers Builds deploy, removed at the commit this search names: it uploaded and promoted a hosted Worker version on each push to main. Its rule that an older commit never wins is kept here, but the job differs: this builds the engine program on a builder and signs a feed entry each computer adopts itself; nothing is uploaded or promoted.
The batching numbers of that removed Worker deploy; this tool's numbers are its own (read-data/settings.json).

This test verifies membership and per-account delivery of signed social event webhooks. It uses the same standard HMAC header, but does not build an engine, sign an Ed25519 release entry or publish a feed.

These carried social event-source definitions describe sender HMAC verification and event routing, including the shared standard signature header. They define incoming social events rather than engine builds or signed release feeds.
The original social event-source DATA describes Meta webhook signatures and event shapes. Its shared HMAC header is transport syntax; it neither builds nor publishes engine releases.

This historical proof sends unsigned and HMAC-signed synthetic Instagram events to an event ingress and checks their acceptance. It is a webhook sender test, not a builder, Ed25519 feed signer or release publisher.
Status documentation of the engine follower and its existing signed release interface. It describes adoption and verification rather than building or publishing a feed.
The engine follower's verification domain, bounds and polling configuration. This is the consuming side of the same release protocol, not a release builder or publisher.

The native engine verifies and adopts releases, including antirollback and private installation. Its signed-byte format is the required interface counterpart; it does not build engines or serve a release feed.
Tests of release verification, target selection, bounded adoption and rollback in the follower. Fixture signatures exercise the consumer protocol rather than an existing publisher implementation.
Integration fixtures sign synthetic feed entries to test a computer forwarding and adopting a release. This is consumer evidence for the wire format, not a reusable build-and-publish algorithm.
The engine build reads the existing release metadata environment variables and embeds them in the program. The publisher must supply that ABI; this build-time consumer does not publish a signed feed.
Documentation of the engine's embedded release identity and the feed it consumes. It names the publisher as its counterpart, not another owner of the publishing job.

The original product DATA describes social webhook sender HMAC verification and event shapes. It shares a standard header with push deliveries but neither builds an engine nor signs or serves Ed25519 release entries.

phrasings: Publish a signed engine release on every push to the branch, so every computer adopts it from a release feed
